title: Large Language Models Substantially Compress Well-Being Inequality but Largely Preserve Its Socioeconomic Structure

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with survey respondent profiles from the World Values Survey to predict life satisfaction, and comparing the variance (inequality) of these predictions across different household income, employment, and education groups against human baseline data to measure representational compression.

Estimating country-specific gradients in well-being inequality from LLM predictions and comparing them to human survey data across 66 countries and territories to evaluate if structural differences between nations are preserved.
